relations.subject: tool:cbcat
relations.evidence: When encryption at rest is active, Couchbase Server encrypts sensitive data stored on disk. This includes logs, configuration files, audit files, and other files generated by Couchbase Server and the services running in the cluster. The `cbcat` tool enables you to decrypt and view the contents of these encrypted files.

relations.evidence: The name and location of the `dump-keys` binary. This binary connects to the keystore and gets the encryption keys. If not specified, the default is `/opt/couchbase/bin/dump-keys`.

relations.subject: tool:cbcat
relations.evidence: A JSON representation of a [keystore](#schema) containing the keys that were used to encrypt the files you want to decrypt and view.

notable_absence.finding: cbcat is the sole tool in this batch with zero RBAC surface: it takes no --username/--password for a Couchbase cluster at all, only a local master password or a locally-supplied JSON keystore. Every other tool here (cbrecovery, cbtransfer, cbworkloadgen, mcstat, mctestauth, mctimings, cbepctl) authenticates against a live cluster with -u/-p. This is a genuine absence rather than an omission - cbcat operates entirely outside the cluster's authorization boundary, on local files, which is worth recording precisely because this round is watching for RBAC-citation consistency and this page has structurally nothing to be inconsistent about.

cross_component_finding: cbcat plugs directly into the already-promoted native-encryption-at-rest key hierarchy (encryption:native-encryption-at-rest, encryption:encryption-at-rest-key) rather than introducing a parallel one - the Key Definition schema's cipher/id/key triple in this page's Schema section is the same object the encryption-at-rest overview and manage pages already describe. No naming drift found between the cli/ page and the learn/manage trees for this feature.
cross_product_finding: The page's own 'Encryption-at-Rest API' See Also link is Couchbase Server's own REST surface for managing encryption keys (rest-api/security/encryption-at-rest/encryption-at-rest.md) - unrelated to the registry's mgmt-api: namespace, which this round's registry excerpt scopes specifically to Capella's management-plane bearer-token credential (mgmt-api:api-key). Correctly not reusing mgmt-api:* here: cbcat and its REST counterpart are Server-only, filesystem-and-keystore-scoped, with no Capella equivalent stated or implied anywhere on the page.
